articles.title: Binance will buy FTX after liquidity crisis rumors
articles.summary: The world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance, has signed a nonbinding letter to acquire the third-largest exchange, FTX. The agreement comes after Twitter beef between the founders.
articles.body: Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange by volume, has signed a letter of intent to buy competitor FTX, the third-largest exchange by volume. The acquisition came after a CoinDesk article prompted speculation about FTX’s balance sheet. The terms of the deal weren’t disclosed. The letter of intent is nonbinding, and Binance CEO Changpeng “CZ” Zhao said the firm will conduct due diligence before the acquisition. Binance’s acquisition came after CZ said on Sunday he’d sell FTX’s FTT token, leading to a plunge in the token’s value. That token was the biggest asset on the balance sheet of Alameda Research, the trading firm also founded by Sam Bankman-Fried, the CEO of FTX, according to CoinDesk’s story. Bankman-Fried said yesterday that CZ’s Binance was attempting to target FTX “with false rumors.” Today, Bankman-Fried said that “rumors in media of conflict between our two exchanges” were exaggerated and that the Binance acquisition will help clear out a backlog of customer withdrawals. Earlier this year, Bankman-Fried rescued BlockFi and Voyager Digital, two troubled crypto lenders that were under threat of bank runs. He’s also cozied up to US lawmakers, donating more than $39 million in this election cycle — still less than he’d promised, which was $1 billion before 2024. By contrast, CZ’s Binance has been targeted by regulators in dozens of countries, including the US. The Securities and Exchange Commission and the Department of Justice in the US are both probing Binance, according to The Wall Street Journal. The deal between the two companies isn’t totally done. “This is a highly dynamic situation, and we are assessing the situation in real time,” CZ said on Twitter. People pulled $1.4 billion from FTX on the Ethereum blockchain over the last day, according to The Wall Street Journal.

articles.title: From Bitcoin to Binance: Crypto terms and what they mean
articles.summary: The Binance hack has thrust cryptocurrencies back into headlines - but what are they and how do they work?
articles.body:
From the rapidly rising and falling values of Bitcoin to high-profile heists like the hacking of Binance , the world of cryptocurrencies is often in the headlines.

The world's biggest crypto exchange said hackers had gained access to $6.3bn (£4.7bn) worth of digital assets, and while it has frozen about half, many remained in the hands of the thieves.

These stories are full of specialist language that people outside the industry struggle to understand.

So if you're unsure what the blockchain or a crypto echange or even a cryptocurrency itself are, here are some key terms and what they mean.

While many may struggle with the finer points of crypto, pretty much everyone has heard of its most famous product: Bitcoin. But what actually is it?

Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is to say a type of digital currency. Unlike traditional currencies, Bitcoin is not controlled by centralised financial institutions.

This makes it popular for people who think decentralisation can bring financial freedom, but it also makes it extremely volatile with it rising and falling in value at the whim of Bitcoin buyers and sellers.

Donald Trump has pledged to make the US the "crypto capital of the world" - backtracking on his previous claim that Bitcoin was a "scam" .

Its price topped a much-awaited threshold of $100,000 in December 2024, then rose to $120,000 in July 2025 as US politicians prepared to debate bills to regulate digital assets.

In October 2025, Bitcoin hit an all-time high of around $126,000, buoyed by a continued wave of institutional investment and positive market sentiment. But it has been known to plummet in value just as quickly as it spikes.

In early February 2026, its price dipped below $65,000 to effectively wipe out gains achieved under President Trump.

Against the backdrop of these frequent price fluctuations, speculation continues about the true identity of Bitcoin's mysterious inventor known only as Satoshi Nakamoto.

Blockchain is the technology underpinning all cryptocurrencies, and many related products like non-fungible tokens (NFTs). In essence, it is a virtual spreadsheet on which all the buying and selling of crypto is recorded. They are arranged in blocks linked together in a giant chain - hence the name.

Every cryptocurrency transaction is individually recorded onto the blockchain by a huge network of volunteers verifying its authenticity by using computer programmes.

The incentive to do this for Bitcoin's network is that the first person to validate transactions is rewarded in Bitcoin. This potentially lucrative process, known as mining, is also controversial because of the incredible amount of energy used as people the world over race to be the first to successfully update the blockchain.

A crypto exchange is the digital platform where investors can buy, sell and trade cryptocurrencies.

Similar to traditional investing, a crypto exchange acts as a brokerage where people can transfer traditional money, like pounds or dollars, in exchange for cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin or Ethereum. Most transactions are accompanied by fees.

Binance is the world's biggest, which is part of what makes the hack so monumental.

A crypto wallet is a place where investors hold their cryptocurrency. There are two types, a hot wallet and a cold wallet.

Hot wallets are connected to the internet, and thus more accessible for quick transfers and easy access.

Cold wallets are physical devices like specially designed USB sticks that store crypto offline typically for safer and longer term storage.

Ethereum is used to describe both the second largest cryptocurrency after Bitcoin, represented by the Ether token, and the blockchain underpinning it. This supports an array of different applications and digital assets, such as non-fungible tokens.

It functions in a similar way to Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, but in 2022 switched to a greener operating system requiring less computers and energy .

ETFs are portfolios that let investors bet on multiple assets without having to buy any themselves. Traded on stock exchanges like shares, their value depends on how the overall portfolio performs in real time. They can comprise a combination of gold and silver bullion, for example, or a mix of shares in both technology and insurance companies.

A spot Bitcoin ETF buys the cryptocurrency directly, "on the spot", at its current price, throughout the day.

While some ETFs already contained Bitcoin indirectly, the US approved several spot Bitcoin ETFs in January 2024. This allowed new investors, such as investment management firms like Blackrock and Fidelity, to enter the speculative world of Bitcoin without having to worry about digital wallets or navigating crypto exchanges.

Meme coins are a form of cryptocurrency used for fun and speculation.

They are typically created to capitalise on social media trends or viral memes - such as for internet-famous pygmy hippo Moo Deng .

But meme coins are heavily criticised for their speculative nature and the risk involved for investors, as they often have little prospect of accumulating value over time.

They can also be susceptible to "rug pulls" - where promoters of a cryptocurrency draw in buyers to raise the price of their coin, only to stop trading activity and make off with the money raised from sales.

Some celebrities have faced backlash after launching meme coins.

"Stable" is the key word here - this cryptocurrency differs from others as it is intends to be less volatile in value.

This typically works by the price being linked to an existing asset, for instance currencies like the US dollar or pound sterling, which in theory should make them more stable in price than cryptocurrencies that are not backed by assets.

Stablecoins themselves are usually controlled by companies that provide them, with transactions recorded on digital ledgers. While held up by some as the future of finance, high profile price collapses of stablecoins have alerted regulators to risks for investors and prompted scrutiny over their supposed stability.

XRP is a cryptocurrency used by a platform called the XRP Ledger. It was created by the co-founders of financial services company Ripple Labs in 2012 as a cheaper, faster alternative to Bitcoin.

The cryptocurrency has a fixed supply of 100 billion coins, which were created when it launched. Much of it is held by Ripple and periodically released into circulation.

Unlike cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin, transactions made using XRP are verified through consensus - whereby the majority of validators on its peer-to-peer network must agree whether or not a transaction is valid before it is added to its blockchain.

This has been credited with allowing many transactions to take place simultaneously, at high speed and low cost - making it appealing to financial institutions or for processes like cross-border payments. But as with other cryptocurrencies, XRP has received regulatory scrutiny and seen sudden, sharp declines in value .

articles.title: Another Trump meme coin contest promises an ‘exclusive’ dinner with the president
articles.summary: The firm behind President Donald Trump’s crypto keepsake known as a meme coin is promoting yet another contest for investors to secure an invitation to “the...
articles.body:
The firm behind President Donald Trump's meme coin is promoting yet another contest for investors to secure an invitation to "the most exclusive dinner in the world" — a sequel to the May 2025 gala that experts called a textbook pay-to-play scandal.

The meme coin's website on Thursday offered "an evening with 3 Legends and President Donald J. Trump" at his private club in Washington , DC , for the top 185 holders of the $TRUMP coin. The top 29 purchasers of the crypto keepsake will be invited to a VIP reception "with YOUR FAVORITE PRESIDENT," and the top four will receive an 18-karat Trump-branded gold watch.

The contest began Wednesday and runs through November 12, according to the site.

At the same time, the site also states that "no attendees will be granted a private meet & greet with the President" and that "no gifts will be accepted." The event is scheduled for November 22.

Early Thursday afternoon, the GetTrumpMemes.co site appeared to crash.

It's the latest episode of Trump and his businesses seemingly profiting off his presidency. Financial disclosures have shown him raking in more than a billion dollars off his crypto ventures and making thousands of stock trades , including in companies that are directly affected by his policies. The White House has repeatedly said Trump is not involved in his investment accounts and that his portfolio "is independently managed by third-party financial institutions."

And it's not the first meme coin event the president has held. The top 220 holders of the $TRUMP meme coin were invited to a black-tie dinner at Trump's golf club outside Washington, DC, in May 2025, with those in the room having contributed millions in investment in his crypto token. The 25 biggest investors also got access to a small VIP reception with the president.

The White House referred questions about the event to the hosts. The companies behind the event, CIC Digital and Fight Fight Fight LLC, are affiliates of the Trump Organization, which didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

Trump has made more than $1 billion from his crypto portfolio, most of which he launched shortly before retaking office in January 2025. Investors in those products have been less fortunate: A report from the watchdog Public Citizen recently tallied investors had racked up $4.7 billion in paper losses on Trump crypto assets managed by the president's adult sons.

Memecoins are particularly risky investments because they have no intrinsic value and are prone to sudden collapses. The US Securities and Exchange Commission last year wrote that memecoins have a failure rate "exceeding 90% for new tokens."

Trump launched his memecoin shortly before his inauguration in 2025. Its value initially surged to $70 but quickly fell. It currently trades around $2.

articles.title: Crypto thieves attacked man in home and threatened to kill pregnant wife's baby in 'horrific' robbery
articles.summary: The man was beaten with hammers until he transferred hundreds of thousands of pounds of cryptocurrency.
articles.body:
Warning: This story contains distressing details

A businessman was beaten with hammers by masked men who broke into his home and threatened to kill his heavily pregnant wife unless he transferred hundreds of thousands of pounds of cryptocurrency.

Speaking to the BBC, the couple, who want to remain anonymous, described the attack as "horrific" and said they feared for their unborn baby's life.

The attackers left in a car driven by a getaway driver after the man transferred his crypto savings.

Crimestoppers are offering a £10,000 reward for information in the attack, which was captured on home security footage and is being investigated by the police.

Experts say it is one of a growing type of violent theft known as a "wrench attack" targeting cryptocurrency investors.

As crypto coins have risen in value, reports of these violent robberies linked to digital assets have emerged in the UK, France and the US.

Once funds are transferred, recovering them can be extremely difficult.

The man, who the BBC is calling James, said three intruders forced their way into their Solihull home before launching an assault which lasted 45 minutes.

"The door gets pushed open, I can see gloves coming in, balaclavas," he said.

James tried to fight the men off but they hit him in the face, head and ribs with hammers.

His wife, who was seven months pregnant, was held down on the sofa by one of the criminals.

"He's got a pillow over her face," James said. "He's literally suffocating her on the sofa. I can hear her screaming, 'I can't breathe'."

The couple still had no idea what the criminals wanted until one of the men demanded James unlock his phone and hand it over.

James said the attackers appeared to know he owned cryptocurrency, but had little understanding of how to access it.

Instead, they were taking instructions from someone else connected via a live video call.

"I can hear the guy on FaceTime saying: 'Show me everything on his phone. Show me what apps he's got'," he said.

When the caller identified a crypto wallet containing substantial funds, the threats escalated dramatically.

"He was basically saying: 'Look, if you don't send us this money now, we're going to stab your wife in the stomach and kill your baby. We're going to kill your wife'," James said.

His wife, who also did not want to be named, described the attack that happened in December last year as "horrific" and said she feared James had been killed when he was unresponsive on the floor.

The woman, in her early thirties, was expecting her third child at the time and said she feared she might lose the baby due to the stress of the attack. The baby survived and was born at full term.

The men left after James transferred his savings - hundreds of thousands of pounds of cryptocurrency - to the digital wallet of the man on the video call.

They also stole several luxury Rolex watches.

James said before they left, he heard the man on the video call tell his accomplices: "You can have 10 grand each but I am taking the rest."

Unlike money held in a conventional bank account, cryptocurrency is often controlled directly by the owner through digital wallets or physical storage devices.

For criminals, that combination of speed, anonymity and irreversibility can make crypto holders attractive targets.

Whilst the vast majority of cryptocurrency theft happens online through hacks and scams, crypto investigators at Chainalysis say "wrench attacks" have surged in recent years.

According to their research, $30m (£22.6m) had been stolen so far this year up to June in violent robberies, making 2026 likely to become the single-worst year for violent crypto attacks on record. Home invasions are also on the rise this year, it found.

The US, Brazil, and Thailand are hotspots but France has seen the largest number of attacks by far, as a result of a data breach at a tax office that has apparently allowed wealthy crypto holders to be located.

"The physical security assumptions that protect traditional wealth, such as bank vaults and armored cars, do not automatically apply in crypto. Often, holders keep their assets in comparatively low security setups, like self-custody wallets, that can be compromised without any institutional gatekeeper standing in the way," said researchers in their report.

James said he became an amateur investor in crypto coins in 2020 and made enough money to quit his job in 2023 to trade full time.

Now he has lost everything and is looking to get back to his traditional job.

Police have yet to identify the attackers.

Crimestoppers is offering a £10,000 reward for information leading to progress in the investigation.

Alan Edwards from the charity hopes people might have information about the three attackers, the driver who was parked outside without a face covering, or the man on the phone.

"These criminals are obviously serious and part of some kind of organised crime gang," he said.

"People might be scared to give us information but we are independent of the police and keep people completely anonymous."

The three attackers are all thought to be in their late teens or early 20s and one of them was a black male with a scar under his left eyebrow.

James said he has little hope of recovering the stolen funds, but instead wanted to see those responsible brought to justice.

He also wants his experience to serve as a warning.

"They threatened my wife and my baby," he said. "People need to understand these risks are real."

articles.title: The Lakers have named their new public address announcer
articles.summary: The Lakers have officially named the successor to Lawrence Tanter, their longtime public address announcer who passed away last week.
articles.body:
For over 40 years, Lawrence Tanter made his mark on the history of the Los Angeles Lakers as their public address announcer at home games, first at The Forum in Inglewood, Calif., and later at Staples Center/Crypto.com Arena. His tenure began during the 1982-83 season and spanned the Showtime era, the Kobe Bryant era and LeBron James' tenure with the franchise.

Tanter missed several games late last season due to a stroke and retired shortly afterward. Last week, it was announced that he had passed away .

The Lakers have now named their official public address announcer for this season. His name is Derrin Horton, and he commented on his new gig, per Benjamin Royer of the Southern California News Group .

"It's a dream," Horton said Thursday, speaking with local media for the first time since taking over for Tanter. "I mean, are you kidding me? The Lakers? … "When I heard about LT and the opportunity here, I reached out and I had a chance to communicate with LT. He was such a legend, and I considered him to be a friend. So now to be here, obviously, there's no way you can fill his shoes, and so you just come here with a passion and a goal to be informative and entertaining and be a part of 'Showtime'."

According to Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times , Horton started out his audition for his new role with the Lakers by trying to imitate Tanter's one-of-a-kind delivery.

"Horton showed up to his audition and instinctively tried to emulate Tanter's signature baritone voice," Nhi Nguyen wrote. "He wanted to sound like what he thought the classic PA announcers should sound like. Lakers president and chief business officer Lon Rosen stopped the tryout in mid-sentence. "'He said, "Hey! articles.title: Ledger wallet tampering suspected after reports of crypto thefts
articles.summary: A spy implant in some Ledger crypto wallets may be the root of an $86 million supply chain attack.
articles.body: Reports have been mounting that users of the Ledger crypto wallet have seen their accounts drained, and it appears to be related to tampered hardware sold by CryptoBillis. Ledger has asked CryptoBillis to pause all sales of its wallets while it conducts an investigation. Ledger has confirmed that “one of the impacted users’ devices contained an unauthorized hardware implant.” Photos and videos posted on X and Threads appear to show a small circuit board sandwiched under the screen. The implant allegedly intercepts anything displayed on the screen, including the seed passphrase shown during the initial setup. Using an embedded SIM card, the implant then sends that information back to the attacker, who can then siphon funds from user accounts. [Media: Reports indicate that whoever is behind the hack has stolen over $86 million worth of crypto from hundreds of wallets. There’s no indication that Ledger’s systems have been compromised or that wallets purchased directly from the company have been affected. Instead, the issue appears to be a supply chain attack primarily involving users in Southeast Asia and the CryptoBillis reseller. Ledger has provided guidance on how to check if your wallet has been tampered with. Update October 10th, 2026: Added additional statment from Ledger.

articles.title: ‘We’ll kill you’: How a late-night cab ride turned into a 15-minute ordeal for Mumbai student
articles.summary: Juhu police arrest 3 within 12 hours for allegedly kidnapping an 18-year-old student in an Uber cab and robbing Rs 14,250 in Mumbai.
articles.body: MUMBAI: An 18-year-old first-year university student has accused three men of kidnapping him in an aggregator cab, driving him around Juhu for 15 minutes, threatening him with a knife and extorting Rs 14,250 before he was let go early on Oct 10.Juhu police registered a case of kidnapping, extortion and robbery against history-sheeters Azad Maniyar (34), Dipesh Chavan (29) and Mondaya Devendra alias Kishan (30) who allegedly forced PA Agarwal into the cab, stole Rs 5,250 from his pocket and compelled him to transfer Rs 9,000 through an e-wallet. They allegedly made Agarwal call his sister before transferring money through UPI.Police caught the three accused at their hideouts in Andheri within 12 hours of the incident involving Agarwal at 1.30 am on Oct 10. “The accused allegedly forced Agarwal into a cab he had booked to return to his PG accommodation, assaulted the driver, forced him inside and sped away. The trio were tracked through technical analysis using the phone number through which money was credited from Agarwal’s account to an e-wallet. Agarwal had earlier gone to drop his aunt’s daughter and her three friends after they had dinner on Oct 9,” said a police officer of the Juhu police station.According to Agarwal’s complaint, three unidentified men allegedly assaulted an Uber driver and forced Agarwal to remain in the car after he dropped his aunt’s daughter and her three friends at a girls’ hostel in Vile Parle (West) around 1.30 am. Agarwal said one man opened the driver’s door, slapped him and questioned where the passengers had come from. The man allegedly told Agarwal there had been a rape at a girls’ hostel in Yenda the previous day and claimed they were union members. Agarwal, who said he was frightened, remained in the car. One of the men, identified by a companion as Azad, allegedly instructed the Uber driver where to drive and took Agarwal around Juhu and other areas. His two companions followed the car on a scooter, the FIR said.Police said Maniyar allegedly threatened Agarwal with a knife near Juhu Ruia Park and forced him to transfer Rs 5,000 to a UPI account. Two accomplices, who had followed them on a scooter, allegedly restrained Agarwal while Maniyar took Rs 5,250 from his trouser pocket. “The group later allegedly forced Agarwal to obtain money from his sister and transfer another Rs 4,000 to the same account. They allegedly threatened to kill him if he disclosed the incident before releasing him near Mithibai College. Agarwal contacted friends and went to lodge a complaint. articles.title: Binance.US Seeks $100 Million to Expand Its Crypto Business
articles.summary: Binance.US is looking to raise as much as $100 million as the crypto exchange seeks to beef up its US business amid intensifying competition for digital-asse...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Binance.US is looking to raise as much as $100 million as the crypto exchange seeks to beef up its US business amid intensifying competition for digital-asset customers.

The company is targeting a valuation of about $1 billion in the private round, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified discussing confidential information.

World Liberty Financial, co-founded by President Donald Trump among others, was among those made aware of the fundraising, according to people familiar with the matter. Another person familiar with the situation said the Trump family's crypto venture isn't participating. The size and valuation of the fundraising, along with the makeup of its investors, could change as the process continues.

Spokespeople for Binance.US and World Liberty declined to comment.

Launched in 2019, Binance.US operates separately from the global Binance exchange, though Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao is a large shareholder of both entities. Binance.US raised more than $200 million in 2022 at a $4.5 billion pre-money valuation.

The latter lost much of its market share following Binance Holdings Ltd.'s 2023 settlement with US authorities and is now seeking to regain ground against larger rivals. The exchange has also explored expanding into new businesses, including prediction markets, Bloomberg News previously reported.

The fundraising bid comes as digital-asset companies seek to capitalize on a more favorable US regulatory environment. Established exchanges are adding products while offshore rivals pursue a larger presence in the country.

Binance.US has discussed the possibility of tapping external sources of trading liquidity, potentially including Binance's international exchange, according to a person familiar with the matter. No approach has been decided, the person said.

Binance.US is also looking to restore some of its state money-transmitting licenses as part of its broader US expansion efforts, according to a person familiar with the matter.

World Liberty already has ties to the global Binance exchange, which holds a lion's share of its USD1 stablecoin, according to the crypto tracker Arkham. The token was also used by an investment firm tied to leaders of the United Arab Emirates to fund its purchase of a $2 billion stake in Binance.

articles.title: Strategy stock falls as Michael Saylor's bitcoin giant faces index-level threat
articles.summary: Strategy stock fell more than 3% on Friday after index provider MSCI announced new eligibility rules that could lead to the removal of Michael Saylor's bitco...
articles.body:
Strategy ( MSTR ) stock fell 8% on Friday after index provider MSCI announced new eligibility rules that could lead to the removal of Michael Saylor's bitcoin juggernaut from its global stock indexes.

MSCI said Thursday it will adopt new rules to exclude certain "non-operating companies" from its indexes, including those whose primary business resembles that of an investment fund rather than a traditional operating company.

Exclusion could include Strategy, the world's largest corporate holder of bitcoin, along with other digital asset treasury companies. Such an action is expected to force index-tracking funds to sell shares of affected companies.

MSCI said it will publish a final list of affected companies on Nov. 11, with the new rules taking effect after the market closes on Nov. 30.

Strategy, led by executive chair Saylor, had previously criticized the proposal as discriminatory against digital asset treasury companies. The company currently holds about 4% of bitcoin's total supply.

On the other hand, Fundstrat head of digital asset strategy Sean Farrell doesn't see Strategy's potential elimination from the index as a significant worry.

"I still think the market can absorb the associated flows," Farrell wrote late Thursday to clients, estimating that selling across MSCI-linked products amounts to "around $2 billion."

"The market has had months to prepare for this outcome. Strategy itself issued more than $2 billion of common stock in August," Farrell added.

Bitcoin's price ( BTC ) fell slightly Friday morning.

articles.title: The Crypto Cop Who Took Down a Global Scam Network from Brooklyn
articles.summary: Crypto scams cost Americans more than $11 billion last year. A Brooklyn prosecutor found a way to hit the networks behind them.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- By the time Alona Katz hurried home from her office in downtown Brooklyn late on Oct. 6, the trap was already set. After months of planning, the chief of Brooklyn's crypto fraud unit was about to orchestrate one of the most sweeping international crackdowns a local prosecutors' office had ever attempted.

The operation, which took place across three time zones, was the culmination of a chase Katz had begun almost as soon as she was appointed chief of Brooklyn District Attorney's Virtual Currency Unit three years ago.

If things went according to plan, Katz would shut down a computer crime network run out of Eastern Europe that had been victimizing Brooklyn residents and had stolen tens of millions of dollars.

The tension grew as the countdown began to start the operation.

"We couldn't entirely control what happened next," Katz said.

At 2 a.m., dozens of computer servers that Katz's team had targeted started going down. She would get no sleep that night.

As crypto use has become more widespread, the global crypto fraud economy has exploded in size. In 2025, reported US losses from cryptocurrency fraud reached $11.4 billion, roughly triple from three years earlier, according to the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

This new frontier of fraud has flummoxed traditional law enforcement agencies, particularly at the local level. Before the Brooklyn DA opened the VCU office, victims who sought help from the New York Police Department were often told to go elsewhere because the NYPD didn't understand the scams, Eric Gonzalez, the Brooklyn District Attorney, said in an interview.

"They would say, 'Go to civil court.' Sometimes they would say, 'Call the FBI, because we don't have the ability to help here because it's an international scam.'"

Federal prosecutors weren't much help either. Most of the fraud targeting citizens in Brooklyn ranges from hundreds to tens of thousands of dollars, significant for the victims but too small to be of interest to the federal authorities, who largely only look into scams of six- or seven-figure dollar amounts, Gonzalez said.

An NYPD spokesperson said its Financial Crimes Task Force investigates cryptocurrency crimes and pointed to a recent case in which the department helped bust a $3.5 million crypto scam. An FBI spokesperson said the agency seeks to prevent crypto fraud through community outreach and working with the private sector.The Black Sheep

articles.title: Bitcoin Rebounds Above $82,000 as Oil's Retreat Lifts Risk Mood
articles.summary: Bitcoin popped back above $82,000 on Monday, rebounding with risk assets as oil prices declined.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) popped back above $82,000 on Monday, rebounding with risk assets as oil prices declined.

The original cryptocurrency climbed as much as 2.3% in early Asia trading and was hovering around $82,400 at noon in Singapore. Smaller tokens also advanced. Ether was up as much as 3.7%, while Solana gained more than 4.6%.

Cryptocurrencies have joined a tentative recovery in risk appetite after oil retreated from a five-month high on signs that supplies from the Middle East have held up since the US war with Iran broke out. Brent crude fell as much as 2%, while a gauge of S&P 500 futures was up roughly 0.8% and Nasdaq 100 futures were up 1.3%.

Improving macro conditions have helped Bitcoin reverse its trend from last week, when it fell roughly 3% along with a selloff in stocks led by technology shares amid renewed doubts about massive spending on artificial intelligence.

Today's move higher is a "retracement after a big risk-off week," said Damien Loh, chief investment officer at Ericsenz Capital.

"No news is good news," he said. "I don't see any near-term drivers for it to break new highs, and I think the risk is for the downside given overall risk environment."

Oil remains elevated at roughly $107 a barrel, higher than prices for most of last week.

Institutional demand has also pulled back from Bitcoin for two consecutive weeks. US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded $228.6 million in outflows last week following $681 million in outflows the previous week.

Bitcoin remains within last week's trading range of $80,000 to $85,000.

articles.title: JPMorgan Asset Sees Bitcoin Beating Stocks, But With a Catch
articles.summary: JPMorgan Asset Management has included Bitcoin in its long-term capital market assumptions for the first time, forecasting returns that could beat stocks, bo...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- JPMorgan Asset Management has included Bitcoin in its long-term capital market assumptions for the first time, forecasting returns that could beat stocks, bonds and gold in a milestone for its Wall Street acceptance.

But there's a catch: Bitcoin's extreme volatility threatens to undermine its appeal on a risk-adjusted basis.

JPMorgan's base case projects annualized returns of 10% over the next decade, but also assumes annual volatility of 55%, more than three times that of US large-cap stocks. The firm stops short of incorporating Bitcoin into its main portfolio models, it said in a report this week, citing its unstable correlations with other assets.

Such volatility can eat into compounded returns as steep losses require even larger gains to recover. That's a risk familiar to Bitcoin ETF investors who bought near the cryptocurrency's peak of just over $126,000 in 2025, only to see their holdings lose as much as 50% as prices retreated.

"We believe it is premature to consider BTC as a diversifier in a balanced portfolio," the JPMorgan team including Tim Lintern, Thushka Maharaj and Sean Daly wrote. "But should volatility continue to decline and correlations to other asset stabilize, this may evolve in the future, particularly as regulation becomes clearer and liquidity and price discovery continue to improve."

Since the pandemic, various Wall Street firms have been making more earnest inroads into the world of cryptocurrencies, shifting from cautious inquiry to more meaningful experimentation that's included making the trading of certain coins available for clients, putting out crypto-focused funds and dabbling with tokenization, among other things.

The JPMorgan analysts say that even as many investors see Bitcoin as a speculative asset, they're still exploring cryptocurrencies — a tenth of clients recently surveyed said their portfolios held crypto, and roughly 17% said they planned to "prioritize crypto." That's thanks, in part, to a regulatory framework that has become more developed and better defined.

Still, Bitcoin right now doesn't cut it as a diversifier in balance portfolios due to its "unstable correlations" to other assets, the bank's researchers said. "If correlations stabilize and volatility declines, BTC's portfolio utility may improve in the future," they wrote.

articles.title: Wall Street brings blockchain into the fold
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS — The buzz at Money 20/20 is focused on consumers being on the verge of near-instant banking transfers, including at night or on weekends, Axios' R...
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS — The buzz at Money 20/20 is focused on consumers being on the verge of near-instant banking transfers, including at night or on weekends, Axios' Ryan Lawler and Lucinda Shen report.

Why it matters: America's financial giants have talked for years about bringing blockchain — the technology that cryptocurrencies like bitcoin are built on — into their systems. Now they're actually doing it.

That shift to instant transfers could also make investing faster and more convenient: Digital versions of stocks could let investors transfer shares around the clock, even when exchanges are closed.

"It's becoming more mainstream institutionally than it ever has been," Digital Currency Group investor Aaron Fu tells Axios, pointing to financial institutions building more blockchain infrastructure in-house.

💡 How it works: Financial institutions have begun using private blockchains to instantly track money and investments as they change hands.

Yes, but: Using the technology behind cryptocurrencies doesn't necessarily mean using the currencies themselves.

Banks can create digital versions of the dollars customers already have on deposit.

💰 State of play: Money 20/20 attendees say that the conversation has moved from "Is this possible?" (the answer is yes) to figuring out exactly how banks will put these services into the electronic hands of consumers like you and me.

The industry group that handles much of the recordkeeping and settlement behind U.S. stock trades is preparing a service that creates digital tokens representing securities held in its system. This is called "tokenization."

Already, Citibank has said its tokenized-deposit service operates in seven markets, letting clients move funds between Citi accounts on a private blockchain.

🔎 Reality check: Competing tokenization efforts could create different versions of the same asset trading on separate networks.

That could confuse investors, reduce liquidity, and make it harder to establish reliable prices.

The bottom line: Blockchain is closer than ever to revolutionizing banking. First, banks, brokers and asset managers must connect systems so consumers and investors can move assets between them as easily as within them.

articles.title: Bitcoin Rallies Back as Tech Rebound Sparks Speculative Appetite
articles.summary: Bitcoin climbed alongside technology stocks as a revival in risk appetite spread to cryptocurrencies, lifting the token out of a bout of listless trading and...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Bitcoin climbed alongside technology stocks as a revival in risk appetite spread to cryptocurrencies, lifting the token out of a bout of listless trading and offering another sign of resurgent speculative fervor across global markets.

The original digital asset rose as much as 2.4% to $84,737 as a rally sparked by SpaceX earnings helped reignite enthusiasm for riskier assets, even as questions lingered over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence boom.

Also helping sentiment: the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency unveiled a final measure for payment stablecoin issuers, in latest sign pro-industry development.

The latest uptick has been in part driven by a rebuilding of leverage via perpetual futures. Open interest, or the total outstanding number of the futures contracts, has been rising again after weeks of deleveraging, according to data compiled by Coinglass.

"Risk assets in general got a lift from solid earnings and renewed AI interest while oil remains elevated and choppy." said Jasper De Maere, an over-the-counter trader at Wintermute. "At the moment, this still feels like a recovery vs the start of a rally, however that could turn quickly if we approach $87,000 Bitcoin with decent momentum."

Besides futures, the crypto options market is posing a bullish posture as well with demand clustered around call contracts at the strike prices of $95,000, $90,000 and $100,000, according to crypto exchange Deribit.

"The longs that were on got cleared out on the way down, and a good part of the bounce was shorts closing. That's largely positioning resetting rather than new leverage going on," said Himanshu Sahay, co-founder of Arch Lending.

Many analysts are monitoring Bitcoin ETF flows for a read on the health of the rally and retail investor involvement. Over the past month, some $2.3 billion has gone into spot funds, data compiled by Bloomberg show, suggesting renewed investor interest. Within the cohort of offerings, BlackRock's IBIT has been the biggest beneficiary, absorbing the majority of those flows during that stretch.

Still, researchers at Glassnode say that though spot ETFs have seen inflows, it hasn't come with heightened trading volume. "Inflows that repeat on rising volume would show demand broadening beyond a single day," they wrote in a note Wednesday.

articles.title: Cryptocurrency companies can keep paying interest-like rewards, say federal bank regulators
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Cryptocurrency companies can continue to pay interest-like rewards to customers, federal regulators said Wednesday, despite warnings from ban...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Cryptocurrency companies can continue to pay interest-like rewards to customers, federal regulators said Wednesday, despite warnings from banks that such programs could drain trillions of dollars in deposits from the banking system.

The new rules are part of the implementation of the GENIUS Act, which was signed into law last year and was meant to codify the rules and regulations around issuers of stablecoins.

Under the rules published by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, stablecoin issuers like Circle will continue to be prohibited from paying interest to people holding their coins. But the exchanges that trade and hold those stablecoins, like Coinbase, Robinhood and others, can pass along any earnings from those coins to customers in interest-like rewards.

Stablecoins are a type of cryptocurrency designed to maintain a steady value, typically $1 per coin. Stablecoins are backed by bank deposits and U.S. Treasuries, which earn interest.

The interest earned from the securities backing stablecoins is at the center of the fight between banks and crypto companies. The cryptocurrency industry wants to offer customers a return on holding stablecoins by converting the interest that stablecoin issuers earn from bonds and dollars backing those coins into a yield for customers.

Under the new OCC rules, exchanges will be able to do so on a "case-by-case basis," regulators said. The practice was not prohibited, as banks had wanted.

Banking groups have pushed for tighter restrictions on stablecoin rewards largely because cryptocurrency companies can and often do offer higher yields on savings than traditional bank accounts. For example, Coinbase offers customers yields of up to 3.5% on USDC balances, whereas the average traditional savings account offers a yield of 0.38%, according to the latest figures from the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp.

If stablecoins and exchanges can outcompete banks on yield, traditional bank customers could move their savings out of banks and into crypto, a phenomenon known as deposit flight. The banking industry has said this would result in banks having a decreased capacity to lend, and in a hypothetical worst-case scenario, cause some banks to close or fail. When lawmakers drafted the CLARITY Act, one source of intense debate was how stablecoins would impact the traditional banking sector.

The American Bankers Association, the umbrella industry lobby group for the industry, said in a statement that the OCC's decision will threaten "the funds banks use to make the loans that drive the U.S. economy."

articles.title: Stablecoins just got the regulatory clarity industry wanted
articles.summary: A federal banking regulator on Wednesday released a final version of new rules on dollar-pegged stablecoins.
articles.body:
A federal banking regulator on Wednesday released a final version of new rules on dollar-pegged stablecoins.

The rules give companies issuing stablecoins more flexibility while leaving a contentious question of stablecoin yield unresolved.

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) finalized rules for implementing the landmark stablecoin legislation President Trump signed into law last year, known as the GENIUS Act. Those rules ease several proposed restrictions on how stablecoin issuers must manage their reserves, including a previous maturity limit that would have prevented issuers from holding longer-term Treasurys.

The OCC, meanwhile, left one of the biggest industry disputes over stablecoins unanswered.

Crypto and banking industry lobbyists squared off earlier this year over whether third-party crypto operators could pay customers yield on their idle stablecoin balances.

Crypto firms have argued that they should have room to compete with banks, while banks have raised concerns that allowing the activity risks deposits being pulled out of the banking system without subjecting the new competition to the same regulatory requirements banks face.

While the GENIUS Act prevents stablecoin issuers from paying interest directly, the OCC eliminated a proposed provision that would have barred crypto exchanges and other third-party platforms from offering customers yield on their idle stablecoin balances.

Instead, the agency said it will evaluate those kinds of arrangements on an individual basis.

TD Cowen policy analyst Jaret Seiberg described the decision as a "negative for banks as it does not fully shut down the ability for platforms to pay yield on stablecoins."

"We see this as creating uncertainty," Seiberg wrote to clients on Wednesday. "It also suggests the Supreme Court ultimately will need to decide what yield payments are legal."

Circle Internet Group ( CRCL ), the country's largest stablecoin issuer, and major crypto exchange Coinbase Global ( COIN ) applauded the new rules. (Disclosure: Yahoo Finance has a partnership with Coinbase.)

"We welcome the OCC's final rules implementing the GENIUS Act — an important milestone in translating America's leadership on stablecoin legislation into clear, durable regulatory standards," Dante Disparte, Circle's chief strategy officer and head of global policy, said in a statement.

"There's a lot to like," Coinbase chief policy officer Faryar Shirzad said in a post on X, referring to the new rules.

articles.title: Trump and Crypto Firm Sued for Profiting From Foreign Government
articles.summary: Donald Trump and World Liberty Financial, the cryptocurrency venture he co-founded with his sons, were sued by a shareholder in a rival crypto firm over clai...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Donald Trump and World Liberty Financial, the cryptocurrency venture he co-founded with his sons, were sued by a shareholder in a rival crypto firm over claims the president illegally profited from his office in violation of the US Constitution.

Benjamin Greenberg, a shareholder in Circle Internet Group Inc., claims illegal competition from World Liberty has harmed him and other Circle investors financially.

The suit claims Trump violated the Foreign Emoluments Clause, a provision of the US Constitution that bars presidents from taking payments from foreign governments without the approval of Congress, in two World Liberty transactions with the United Arab Emirates.

"This action is about the President of the United States corruptly profiting from more than $2 billion in payments from a foreign government in direct violation of the Constitution," Greenberg said in a complaint filed Thursday in federal court in Washington. "No president in American history has profited from his office so brazenly."

Trump reported $1.4 billion in earnings related to his crypto ventures, including World Liberty, last year. The revelation drew a backlash from Democrats in Congress and has been blamed in part for the failure of the Clarity Act, which was supposed to establish market-structure rules for the crypto industry.

According to Greenberg, the sale of a 49% stake in World Liberty for $500 million to an investment vehicle backed by a member of UAE's ruling family and the purchase by Abu Dhabi's MGX fund of World Liberty's stablecoin to fund a $2 billion transaction were against US law.

Greenberg filed his so-called derivative complaint as an individual Circle shareholder seeking to recover damages on the company's behalf. He claims shareholders were financially harmed by World Liberty, which competes with Circle in the stablecoin market.

"This lawsuit was filed by an individual shareholder, not by Circle," a company spokesperson said in response to the suit. "Circle did not initiate, direct, authorize, or participate in the filing."

A World Liberty spokesperson said the claims are "without merit."

"World Liberty Financial is compliant with all US laws and regulations," David Wachsman said in a statement. "No one at World Liberty Financial works for the US government."

articles.title: More than $1.4 billion has been traded on prediction markets for the 2026 midterms
articles.summary: Prediction markets about the 2026 midterm elections have surpassed $1.4 billion in trading volume as Election Day fast approaches, according to a new CNN ana...
articles.body:
Prediction markets about the 2026 midterm elections have surpassed $1.4 billion in trading volume as Election Day fast approaches, according to a new CNN analysis.

This year has seen massive growth in the prediction industry , where people can bet on real-world events like sports, entertainment and the weather. While small-scale election markets have been around for a while, they gained traction before the 2024 presidential election and have seen huge numbers for the 2026 midterms.

Kalshi, the biggest US prediction company, has seen nearly $1.1 billion in trading volume on markets related to the midterms, according to a spokesperson. This includes markets about individual race outcomes, turnout numbers, prominent endorsements, whether candidates will debate, what will be said at campaign rallies and much more.

Its rival Polymarket has seen more than $340 million in trading volume on midterm-related markets, a spokesperson told CNN. This includes trading on Polymarket's US-facing platform as well as its offshore site that's popular with international users.

"It's sizable," said Dustin Gouker, an industry expert who writes a newsletter about prediction markets. "It's still much less than sports and crypto markets, but it's a lot of trading. And it's valuable. It's a meaningful signal that provides probabilities that aggregate polls and public sentiment."

Gouker said trading is expected to significantly ramp up on Election Day, as professional bettors try to cash in on volatile changes in the markets while polls close across the country.

Still, as with gambling, most people who trade on prediction markets lose money .

The prediction frenzy has scrambled US political culture, with campaign staffers and donors obsessing over the odds. Federal regulators have pledged to crack down on insider trading related to the midterms, and Kalshi has already suspended six 2026 candidates for improperly betting on their own races.

Trading volume does not measure how much money has been wagered on a specific market. These figures capture the overall economic activity, in terms of how much money has changed hands before the market have been closed.

CNN has a partnership with Kalshi and uses its data to cover major events. But CNN editorial employees aren't allowed to trade on prediction markets.

PredictIt, which bills itself as the "original political prediction market," has been around since 2014. The company declined to provide dollar figures for its 2026 midterms trading volume, but co-founder John Aristotle Phillips said business has been growing because of the favorable regulatory climate.

articles.title: Netanyahu Says Israel Mulls Crypto Ahead of Possible Sanctions
articles.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu said he is exploring the use of cryptocurrency to circumvent potential financial sanctions on Israel, drawing criticism from opposition fi...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Benjamin Netanyahu said he is exploring the use of cryptocurrency to circumvent potential financial sanctions on Israel, drawing criticism from opposition figures who said it would turn the Jewish state into an economic pariah like Iran.

"We need to prepare ways to evade banking sanctions through an alternative economic system," the prime minister said in an interview with Israel's Channel 10. "You know what that means — the currencies that can bypass them. I'm working on that too." Asked whether he meant crypto, the prime minister said: "Very correct."

Netanyahu was speaking ahead of the Oct. 27 election, where he faces a strong challenge from former general Gadi Eisenkot.

Opposition leader Yair Lapid said the prime minister's proposal for evading potential sanctions "belongs to countries like Iran, Russia, and Venezuela — nations whose banks are cut off from the world, whose companies cannot accept payments, and whose young people are fleeing."

"That's his vision," Lapid added in a post on X.

Last month, 12 major countries led by the UK pledged coordinated measures against Israeli settlements in the West Bank. UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the moves would also cover individuals and companies providing financing, construction and other services to the settlements.

That raised fears of sanctions on Israeli banks that could rattle the tech-export-driven economy.

"The concern is that foreign banks will cease providing correspondent services to their Israeli counterparts, effectively severing Israel's ability to conduct international economic activity," said Yair Avidan, a former banking supervisor at the Bank of Israel.

Netanyahu "is finally admitting that Israel faces a real danger of diplomatic isolation and economic sanctions, yet instead of explaining how he intends to prevent them, he is already talking about preparing a 'sanctions-bypassing economy,'" said former Finance Minister Avigdor Liberman, leader of Israel Beytenu, an opposition party. He vowed to "break Israel out of diplomatic isolation and eliminate the threat of sanctions" if the opposition takes power.

In the interview, Netanyahu also warned that decades of US military aid would end, forcing Israel to finance its defense on its own.

articles.title: NC woman lost all her savings at a gas-station bitcoin machine. A new law could force refunds — but not until January
articles.summary: Attorney General Jeff Jackson says an investigation is underway. New protections come with strings attached. Here's what the law covers and how kiosk scams w...
articles.body:
The callers said they were local police, and that her cash would buy her safe release from custody. So a woman in Johnston County, North Carolina, fed her savings into a cryptocurrency kiosk at a gas station.

Only when the callers demanded another $4,000 and she told them she had nothing left did the line go dead and the truth sink in, WRAL reported .

Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP

The tax breaks in Trump's 'big beautiful bill' expire after 2028. Here are 4 reasons why retirees can't afford to waste time

Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

"I just set up an appointment with a counselor, so I'd have somebody to talk to, because it's really hurt me financially and hurt me mentally," she told the station. She asked not to be identified.

North Carolina Attorney General Jeff Jackson said the U.S. Department of Justice is looking into kiosk companies. "Investigation [is] underway as we speak," he told WRAL.

Crypto kiosks look like regular ATMs but turn cash into cryptocurrency. Transfers happen almost instantly, leave little evidence and are hard to reverse, WRAL reports .

And the number of scams is climbing. The FBI said that kiosk complaints topped 13,400 in 2025, up 23% from 2024, with reported losses of more than $388 million, up 58%. More than half the complaints involved people over 50. For North Carolina, the alert lists 491 complaints and about $12.6 million in losses.

Back in 2023, the FBI counted more than 5,500 kiosk complaints and $189 million in losses.

And the Federal Trade Commission found that losses at bitcoin ATMs grew almost tenfold from 2020 to 2023. In the first half of 2024, the median reported loss was $10,000, and people 60 and older were more than three times as likely as younger adults to report a loss.

Governor Josh Stein signed House Bill 920 in July. He said the law protects people from fraud at virtual currency kiosks by requiring the machines to be licensed and regulated under state law, limiting daily transactions and providing scam alert signs, live customer service, receipts and the ability to cancel an in-progress transaction. The law takes effect Jan. 1, 2027.

articles.title: Is Binance Being Hacked? $2 Billion Outflow Puts Customer Funds in Question
articles.summary: Over $2 billion left Binance hot wallets to a Tornado Cash-funded address. Are customer funds safe? What the chain shows.
articles.body:
More than $2 billion in Ethereum (ETH) and tokens left Binance hot wallets on Thursday for an address created hours earlier and funded through Tornado Cash, Etherscan data shows. Binance has not said whether customer deposits are at risk.

The money in those wallets belongs to Binance users, and a confirmed theft would dwarf the $387 million Bitget hack in September. If it was routine housekeeping, the exchange moved its reserves along a path that mirrors how hackers cover their tracks.

At 20:24 UTC on October 29, one transaction moved 167,464 ETH, worth about $388 million by Etherscan's valuation, out of the wallet labeled Binance 14. It also pushed 63 tokens to the receiving address, including roughly $1.6 billion in Tether (USDT).

A second exchange wallet, Binance 16, sent another 28,005 ETH to the same address 24 seconds later.

The receiving address did not exist before Thursday. Within 15 minutes it forwarded 195,460 ETH, around $450 million, to yet another fresh address while still holding about $1.5 billion in tokens.

The transfer was triggered by a wallet funded only through Tornado Cash, a mixing service that hides where coins come from. That wallet took three deposits of roughly 0.1 ETH on October 28 and 29.

A hot wallet is one an exchange keeps online to pay withdrawals, and exchanges do shuffle funds between them. Spreek, a pseudonymous on-chain researcher, flagged the transfer on X.

"It COULD be routine wallet maintenance, but it looks extremely sus"

Tree News, a market alert feed, put the outflow at about $2.53 billion across more than 60 tokens and labeled it a suspected key compromise, meaning someone other than Binance may control the wallet.

Two details weigh against the maintenance reading. A Binance-run transfer has no reason to start from a mixer-seeded wallet. The receiving address also split the funds onward at once, a pattern seen in the Bitget hack timeline after the stolen coins moved.

Binance keeps customer assets in these wallets, so a confirmed key compromise would test whether its emergency reserve fund can absorb a loss this size.

A Binance spokesperson told BeInCrypto by email that the exchange is "aware of reports of a potential security issue" and is investigating, adding that it has "not confirmed any impact to user funds" and will post updates through official channels.

Update (October 30, 00:30 UTC): Binance founder Changpeng Zhao said on X that the transfer "does look like a hack on Binance" and that he expects user funds to be fully covered. Tether chief executive Paolo Ardoino said the firm froze more than 1.567 billion USDT linked to the incident, and Zhao put Circle's USDC freeze near $823 million. Users have also reported withdrawals stuck at processing.

articles.title: Hackers roubam R$ 34 bilhões da Binance, maior corretora de cripto | G1
articles.standfirst: Ataque, considerado o maior da história do setor, teria sido realizado por hackers da Coreia do Norte. Empresa afirma que vai cobrir os prejuízos e que o dinheiro dos clientes está protegido.
articles.summary: Ataque à Binance pode ser o maior roubo de criptomoedas da história. Hackers ligados à Coreia do Norte são suspeitos; empresa promete cobrir as perdas.
articles.body:
A Binance, maior corretora de criptomoedas do mundo, foi alvo de um ataque hacker que resultou no roubo de US$ 6,3 bilhões (cerca de R$ 34 bilhões) . Segundo especialistas, essa foi a maior ação criminosa já registrada na história do setor. A ação aconteceu na quinta-feira (29) e levou aproximadamente 20 minutos.

Fundada em 2017 em Xangai, na China, a Binance é uma plataforma que permite comprar, vender e guardar criptomoedas, como o Bitcoin.

Segundo seu relatório anual de 2025, a empresa tem 335 milhões de usuários cadastrados em todo o mundo e mantinha sob sua responsabilidade cerca de US$ 162,8 bilhões (R$ 879 bilhões) em ativos digitais.

O ataque levantou preocupações sobre a segurança dessas plataformas e provocou uma queda no preço das principais criptomoedas nesta sexta-feira (30). ( veja mais abaixo )

Segundo as empresas americanas TRM Labs e Chainalysis, especializadas em rastrear movimentações de criptomoedas, os responsáveis pelo roubo seriam hackers ligados à Coreia do Norte. A Binance, porém, afirmou que sua investigação ainda não identificou os criminosos.

A corretora suspendeu temporariamente os saques, mas garantiu que o dinheiro dos clientes está protegido e prometeu cobrir todas as perdas.

Segundo a Reuters, a Binance está trabalhando com autoridades policiais em todo o mundo, incluindo o Departamento Federal de Investigação (FBI, na sigla em inglês) e o Serviço Secreto dos Estados Unidos (USSS).

A expectativa é que o serviço seja retomado nas próximas 45 horas, segundo a atualização divulgada pela empresa.

Até agora, cerca de US$ 3 bilhões (R$ 16,2 bilhões) em criptomoedas roubadas foram localizados. Parte desses recursos já foi bloqueada com a ajuda de outras empresas do setor, mas isso não significa que o dinheiro tenha sido recuperado.

Como os hackers conseguiram roubar tanto dinheiro?

As investigações ainda estão em andamento, mas as primeiras informações ajudam a entender como os criminosos conseguiram desviar uma quantia tão elevada em poucos minutos. ( veja mais aqui )

Inicialmente, a Binance suspeitou que o ataque tivesse começado pelo computador de um de seus engenheiros. O equipamento teria sido invadido, permitindo que os hackers entrassem nos sistemas da empresa.

Posteriormente, a corretora informou que encontrou outras falhas de segurança que também podem ter sido exploradas.

Segundo a TRM Labs, os criminosos conseguiram comprometer o sistema responsável por autorizar transferências de criptomoedas.

A maior parte do roubo aconteceu em aproximadamente 20 minutos , por volta das 17h (horário de Brasília), segundo registros das transações analisados por especialistas.

Após o desvio, os criminosos começaram a movimentar rapidamente os recursos para dificultar o bloqueio e o rastreamento do dinheiro.

O que aconteceu com os R$ 34 bilhões roubados?

Uma das principais dúvidas é se a Binance conseguirá recuperar o dinheiro.

Até o momento, a corretora informou ter localizado cerca de US$ 3 bilhões (R$ 16,2 bilhões) , enquanto a situação dos outros US$ 3,3 bilhões (R$ 17,8 bilhões) ainda não foi totalmente esclarecida.

Parte dos valores roubados estava em stablecoins , um tipo de criptomoeda criado para manter um preço estável, geralmente equivalente ao dólar.

🔍 Diferentemente do Bitcoin, algumas dessas moedas digitais podem ser bloqueadas pelas empresas responsáveis por sua emissão. Isso significa que, mesmo depois de roubadas, elas podem ficar impedidas de ser transferidas ou utilizadas pelos criminosos.

Foi o que aconteceu com parte dos recursos desviados da Binance.

A Tether, uma das maiores empresas desse mercado, informou ter congelado quase US$ 1,57 bilhão (R$ 8,5 bilhões) .

A Circle bloqueou mais de US$ 800 milhões (R$ 4,3 bilhões) , enquanto a Ripple congelou aproximadamente US$ 200 milhões (R$ 1,1 bilhão) .

A World Liberty Financial , empresa de criptomoedas ligada ao presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, e à sua família, também participou das ações para bloquear recursos, segundo a Reuters.

💰 Embora parte dos recursos roubados tenha sido bloqueada, ainda não há garantia de que o dinheiro será recuperado. Isso porque o congelamento impede que os hackers movimentem as criptomoedas, mas não significa que os valores tenham sido devolvidos à Binance.

Além disso, criptomoedas como Bitcoin e Ether não possuem uma empresa central capaz de bloquear diretamente as transferências.

Segundo a TRM Labs, cerca de US$ 2,4 bilhões (R$ 13 bilhões) em Bitcoin e Ether podem estar fora do alcance imediato das medidas de bloqueio.

Os especialistas explicam que esses recursos só poderiam ser interceptados em determinadas situações, como quando os criminosos tentassem transferi-los para uma corretora disposta a bloquear as operações.

As empresas americanas TRM Labs e Chainalysis apontam que o roubo apresenta características semelhantes às de ataques realizados anteriormente por hackers ligados à Coreia do Norte.

Uma das principais semelhanças é com a invasão à corretora Bybit, em 2025, atribuída pelo FBI, a polícia federal dos Estados Unidos, a criminosos norte-coreanos. Segundo a TRM Labs, é possível que o mesmo grupo esteja envolvido no ataque à Binance

A Coreia do Norte é acusada há anos por autoridades americanas e sul-coreanas de utilizar grupos de hackers para roubar recursos e financiar atividades do governo. O país nega as acusações.

Apesar das suspeitas, a Binance ressaltou que ainda não conseguiu identificar oficialmente os responsáveis pela invasão.

A Binance afirmou que os recursos dos clientes estão seguros e que vai cobrir todos os prejuízos provocados pelo ataque hacker.

Segundo a corretora, os depósitos não foram afetados e a previsão é que os serviços de saque sejam retomados em até 45 horas, conforme a atualização divulgada pela empresa.

Para compensar as perdas, a Binance informou que utilizará recursos próprios e um fundo de emergência criado para proteger os clientes em casos de falhas de segurança.

Conhecido como SAFU, esse fundo possui uma reserva de aproximadamente US$ 1 bilhão (R$ 5,4 bilhões) em Bitcoin . O valor, porém, é muito inferior aos US$ 6,3 bilhões (R$ 34 bilhões) desviados pelos criminosos.

Em publicação na rede social X, a corretora informou que a investigação inicial apontava para a invasão do computador de um funcionário, mas que novas apurações identificaram outras possíveis falhas de segurança.

A empresa também afirmou que está trabalhando com autoridades e parceiros para investigar o ataque e impedir que os criminosos movimentem os recursos desviados.

"Este foi um ataque complexo e estamos fazendo tudo o que podemos, em coordenação com as autoridades, para resolvê-lo", afirmou a corretora.

A notícia do roubo provocou uma reação negativa no mercado de criptomoedas nesta sexta-feira (30).

Por volta das 12h, o Bitcoin, a moeda digital mais conhecida do mundo, caiu mais de 5% e chegou a US$ 77.212,6 (cerca de R$ 416,9 mil) , seu menor valor em seis semanas.

No mesmo horário, o Ether , segunda maior criptomoeda do mercado, também recuou mais de 5%, atingindo US$ 2.245,39 (cerca de R$ 12,1 mil) , o menor patamar em dois meses.

Já o BNB , criptomoeda ligada à Binance e utilizada para pagar taxas na plataforma, caiu 6% em 24 horas, para US$ 700,80 (cerca de R$ 3,8 mil) .

O impacto também chegou ao mercado de ações dos Estados Unidos. Os papéis da Coinbase , outra grande corretora de criptomoedas, recuaram 4,8%.

As ações da Strategy , empresa conhecida por manter grandes investimentos em Bitcoin, caíram quase 6% nas negociações após o fechamento regular das bolsas americanas.

A Coinbase afirmou que não foi afetada pela invasão e que continua acompanhando o caso.

Outros roubos bilionários já atingiram o setor

O ataque à Binance é o mais recente de uma série de grandes invasões contra empresas de criptomoedas.

Somente em 2025, criminosos roubaram aproximadamente US$ 2,9 bilhões (R$ 15,7 bilhões) em quase 150 ataques, segundo levantamento da TRM Labs ( veja os maiores ataques já registrados ) .

Em setembro deste ano, a corretora Bitget informou ter sofrido um roubo de aproximadamente US$ 350 milhões (R$ 1,9 bilhão) .

O logotipo da Binance é visto em um smartphone, em 28 de fevereiro de 2023, em Marple Township, Pensilvânia. — Foto: Matt Slocum/AP

articles.title: Após ataque hacker bilionário, Binance diz que investimentos de brasileiros estão seguros | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresa afirma que investimentos dos clientes brasileiros estão protegidos, mas mantém saques suspensos enquanto realiza verificações de segurança. Especialistas explicam os riscos para investidores.
articles.summary: Saques na corretota continuam temporariamente suspensos. Especialistas explicam os riscos para investidores.
articles.body:
A corretora de criptomoedas Binance afirmou nesta sexta-feira (30) que os investimentos de seus clientes brasileiros permanecem seguros após o ataque hacker que resultou no roubo de US$ 6,3 bilhões (cerca de R$ 34 bilhões) em criptomoedas . ( leia o comunicado na íntegra mais abaixo )

Em comunicado, a empresa explicou que os ativos dos clientes no Brasil são mantidos em cold wallets , conhecidas como carteiras frias, e que segue as regras do Banco Central do Brasil (BC), que exigem a separação dos recursos dos usuários daqueles pertencentes à corretora.

🔎 Cold wallet, ou carteira fria, é uma forma de guardar criptomoedas que mantém as chaves necessárias para movimentá-las desconectadas da internet. Isso dificulta a ação de hackers e reduz o risco de roubos virtuais, mas não elimina completamente a possibilidade de perdas.

Apesar da garantia de segurança, os saques de criptomoedas estão temporariamente suspensos. Segundo a Binance, a medida é preventiva e permite a realização de uma análise dos sistemas da plataforma.

A corretora informou que segue dentro do cronograma para restabelecer o serviço em até 45 horas. Os depósitos não foram afetados, e os demais serviços continuam funcionando normalmente.

“A segurança dos ativos virtuais de nossos clientes continua sendo nossa maior prioridade”, afirmou a Binance.

Pelas regras do Banco Central, em vigor desde fevereiro deste ano, as corretoras de criptomoedas devem manter o dinheiro e os ativos digitais dos clientes separados dos recursos da própria empresa .

A exigência, porém, não elimina o risco de ataques hackers nem garante o ressarcimento de eventuais perdas.

Investidores brasileiros ainda podem perder dinheiro?

André Matos, CEO da MA7 Capital, explica que, neste momento, o principal risco para os clientes da Binance é ficar temporariamente sem acesso aos recursos, e não a perda definitiva.

A corretora prometeu cobrir os prejuízos provocados pelo ataque utilizando seu fundo de emergência, recursos próprios e valores roubados que já foram bloqueados.

Segundo Matos, porém, a capacidade da empresa de arcar com todas as perdas ainda não foi comprovada de forma independente.

"Há ainda um ponto que muita gente não percebe: a promessa cobre os ativos roubados, não a queda de preço", afirma.

Isso significa que os investidores também podem perder dinheiro com a desvalorização das criptomoedas , mesmo que seus ativos não tenham sido diretamente atingidos pelo ataque.

Diferentemente dos depósitos bancários e de determinados investimentos de renda fixa, as criptomoedas não contam com a proteção do Fundo Garantidor de Créditos (FGC).

Celso Camilo, doutor em Inteligência Artificial pela Universidade Federal de Goiás (UFG), ressalta que o ataque não significa que todos os investidores em criptomoedas terão seus recursos comprometidos.

"Estamos falando da maior corretora de criptoativos do mundo, e um incidente dessa dimensão afeta diretamente a confiança dos investidores. Quem mantém recursos na Binance enfrenta uma exposição mais direta ao problema, principalmente em relação à segurança dos ativos e à disponibilidade de saques", afirma.

Segundo Camilo, quem investe por outras plataformas não está necessariamente exposto ao ataque, mas pode sentir os efeitos da queda dos preços.

"Portanto, é importante separar o risco de perder recursos em uma plataforma do risco de desvalorização dos ativos, que atinge o mercado de maneira mais ampla."

Após a divulgação do ataque hacker, o mercado de criptomoedas reagiu em forte queda nesta sexta-feira.

Por volta das 14h24 (horário de Brasília), o Bitcoin e o Ether caíam mais de 4%, cotados a US$ 77.274,30 (cerca de R$ 417,3 mil) e US$ 2.245,39 (cerca de R$ 12,1 mil) , respectivamente.

Já o BNB , criptomoeda ligada à Binance, recuava 6%, para US$ 700,80 (R$ 3,8 mil).

As perdas também atingiram o mercado de ações dos Estados Unidos. Os papéis da Coinbase, outra grande corretora de criptomoedas, recuavam mais de 13%, enquanto os da Strategy, empresa conhecida por seus investimentos em Bitcoin, caíam mais de 8% nesta tarde.

Os fundos de criptomoedas negociados na B3 também registravam perdas, em meio à repercussão do ataque hacker à Binance.

Por volta das 12h40, o HASH11 , que acompanha uma cesta de moedas digitais, recuava 2,64% , enquanto o QBTC11 , atrelado ao Bitcoin, caía 3,94% .

Como saber se o dinheiro está exposto à Binance?

Segundo André Matos, o primeiro passo é verificar onde as criptomoedas estão armazenadas e quem é responsável por protegê-las.

"Se elas estão na sua conta da Binance, você está exposto, porque quem tem a custódia é a corretora. Se estão em uma carteira própria, em que só você tem as chaves, o ataque não atinge esses ativos diretamente, embora o preço possa cair."

Para quem investe por bancos, fundos ou outros aplicativos, a recomendação é verificar qual instituição guarda os ativos e quais plataformas são utilizadas nas operações.

O que os investidores devem fazer agora?

Embora os recuros ainda estejam bloqueados para quem investe na Binance, Matos recomenda evitar decisões precipitadas, reforçar a segurança das contas e ficar atento a possíveis golpes.

"O mais importante é não agir no pânico. Vender na baixa ou tentar sacar a qualquer custo pode transformar um problema temporário em prejuízo definitivo."

O especialista recomenda que os investidores:

Guardem os comprovantes dos investimentos;

Desconfiem de mensagens que prometam liberar saques em troca de senhas ou dados pessoais.

Para reduzir riscos no futuro, ele também recomenda não concentrar todos os investimentos em uma única corretora.

"Quem pretende manter as criptomoedas por muito tempo deve considerar uma carteira própria, de preferência física, tomando muito cuidado para guardar as palavras de recuperação."

🔎 Uma carteira física é um dispositivo que permite ao investidor guardar as chaves de acesso às criptomoedas fora da internet, sem depender de uma corretora.

Para recuperar o acesso aos recursos em caso de perda ou defeito do aparelho, é necessário guardar uma sequência de palavras de segurança. Se essas palavras forem perdidas ou caírem nas mãos de criminosos, o investidor pode ficar sem suas criptomoedas.

O ataque à Binance ocorreu na quinta-feira (29) e é considerado o maior roubo já registrado na história do setor de criptomoedas.

Segundo as empresas americanas TRM Labs e Chainalysis, especializadas em rastrear movimentações de criptomoedas, os responsáveis seriam hackers ligados à Coreia do Norte.

A Binance, porém, afirmou que sua investigação ainda não identificou os criminosos.

De acordo com a Reuters, a corretora está trabalhando com autoridades policiais de diferentes países, incluindo o Departamento Federal de Investigação (FBI, na sigla em inglês) e o Serviço Secreto dos Estados Unidos (USSS).

Até agora, cerca de US$ 3 bilhões (R$ 16,2 bilhões) em criptomoedas roubadas foram localizados. Parte desses recursos foi bloqueada com a ajuda de outras empresas do setor, mas isso não significa que o dinheiro tenha sido recuperado.

As investigações ainda estão em andamento, mas as primeiras informações ajudam a entender como os criminosos conseguiram desviar uma quantia tão elevada em poucos minutos.

Inicialmente, a Binance suspeitou que o ataque tivesse começado pelo computador de um de seus engenheiros. O equipamento teria sido invadido, permitindo que os hackers acessassem os sistemas da empresa. ( veja mais aqui )

Posteriormente, a corretora informou que identificou outras possíveis falhas de segurança exploradas pelos criminosos.

Segundo a TRM Labs, os invasores conseguiram comprometer o sistema responsável por autorizar transferências de criptomoedas.

A maior parte do roubo aconteceu em aproximadamente 20 minutos, por volta das 17h (horário de Brasília), segundo registros das transações analisados por especialistas.

Após o desvio, os criminosos começaram a movimentar rapidamente os recursos para dificultar o bloqueio e o rastreamento do dinheiro.

"Diante das notícias recentes sobre o incidente de segurança envolvendo a Binance Global, a BBrasil SPSAV LTDA., entidade da Binance que atende os usuários brasileiros, confirma que os fundos de seus clientes permanecem seguros. Além de observar os requisitos de segregação estabelecidos pelo Banco Central do Brasil, os ativos virtuais são mantidos em cold wallets (carteiras frias), agregando uma camada adicional de segurança e reforçando o compromisso da BBrasil SPSAV com a proteção dos ativos de seus clientes.

Como medida preventiva e conforme informado anteriormente, os saques de ativos virtuais estão temporariamente suspensos enquanto realizamos uma verificação minuciosa de segurança. Todos os demais serviços da plataforma continuam funcionando normalmente, e retomaremos as operações de saque assim que o processo de verificação for concluído.

A segurança dos ativos virtuais de nossos clientes continua sendo nossa maior prioridade. Permanecemos plenamente comprometidos com a manutenção de padrões rigorosos de segurança para garantir a total confiança de todos os nossos clientes.

Pedimos sinceras desculpas por qualquer inconveniente causado."
